cards.explanation: The answer is God our Savior and Christ Jesus. Paul says he's an apostle of Christ Jesus "…by the command of God our Savior and of Christ Jesus our hope…" (1 Timothy 1:1). Paul isn't saying he picked the job himself. He says it came by their command, and friends, that's a pretty strong way to open a letter.

The city is Ephesus! Paul says he urged Timothy to "…stay on at Ephesus…" when he left for Macedonia (1 Timothy 1:3). Timothy had a job to do there, and Paul wanted him in place to do it. Staying put can be real work, friends.

The answer is teaching false doctrines. Paul wants Timothy "…to instruct certain men not to teach false doctrines" (1 Timothy 1:3). The myths and genealogies come right after that in verse 4. So there's a whole pile of things to stop, friends, and false teaching is the first one named.

The word is speculation. Paul says the myths and endless genealogies "…promote speculation rather than the stewardship of God’s work, which is by faith." (1 Timothy 1:4). Speculation is just guessing that goes around and around. Stewardship of God's work, though, is by faith.

The word is love, friends. Paul says "The goal of our instruction is the love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience, and a sincere faith." (1 Timothy 1:5). All that teaching is aiming at love. Not at winning, and not at sounding smart.

The answer is False. Paul says "They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or that which they so confidently assert." (1 Timothy 1:7). They want to teach the law, friends, but they don't understand what they're saying. And they say it with confidence anyway!

The answer is that the law is good if used rightly. Paul says "…the law is good, if one uses it legitimately." (1 Timothy 1:8). Good is his word for the law, friends. What matters is that it's used the legitimate way.

The answer is False. Paul says "…law is not enacted for the righteous, but for the lawless and rebellious…" (1 Timothy 1:9). So the law isn't aimed at the righteous, friends. It's aimed at the lawless and rebellious, and the list that follows spells out who he means.

The answer is the glorious gospel of the blessed God. Paul says sound teaching "…agrees with the glorious gospel of the blessed God, with which I have been entrusted." (1 Timothy 1:10-11). That's the measuring stick, friends. Teaching that doesn't line up with the gospel isn't sound.

The answer is True! Paul says the glorious gospel is the one "…with which I have been entrusted." (1 Timothy 1:11). Being handed something that important is a big deal, friends. I think Paul felt the weight of that.
